text:
sasha: Heads-up — after landing kernel-selector fallback + async KV prewarm I'm seeing a throughput regression on 1F1B runs. PP bubble widened, all-reduce wait times up ~35% on 8-GPU perf cluster. Anyone else notice this?

devon: Which model/config? can you paste the lightweight trace/snippets?

sasha: gpt-medium-8b, tp=2, pp=4. Repro steps: microbatch sweep 8->16. Quick nvprof/pprof extract below (trimmed):
```
NCCL_ALLREDUCE wait 0.43s -> 0.58s
kernel_selector: chosen=quant_kernels_v2 (fallback engaged)
KV_CACHE hits 0.95 -> 0.60 on first 10 steps
1F1B idle tail per-stage +0.12s
```

cheng: hm — looks like two orthogonal issues: KV misses are increasing early, and kernel fallback is picking kernels with higher launch latency. Combined they can blow up the 1F1B overlap.

kevin: NCCL version? we saw similar tail with 2.16.x on machines with mixed NVLink/PCIe. Also check driver + cta size changes from the new kernels.

sasha: NCCL 2.16.2, driver 535. KV prewarm is async (fire-and-forget), which might be racing with the first few microbatches and creating more synchronization points.

maria: Quick experiment: try reducing microbatch to 4 + synchronous KV prewarm + disable kernel-fallback. Small command I ran locally: 
```
runtest --model gpt-8b --tp 2 --pp 4 --microbatch 4 --profile=timeline --disable-kernel-fallback --kv-prewarm=sync
```

devon: I'll spin that on the infra rig now and capture NCCL traces (NCCL_DEBUG=INFO + NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=ALL).

sasha: :thumbsup: also can we dump per-kernel launch times? I want to see whether launch latency or kernel runtime dominates the new tails.

cheng: If launch latency is the culprit, two mitigations to try: 1) staggered 1F1B warmup (give earlier stages a head-start so their all-reduces overlap better), 2) split-reduce: break large all-reduce into two smaller ops to reduce tail variance (we have an experimental patch in branch pp/split-reduce).

kevin: Another angle — persistent kernel/persistent-thread mode can amortize launch cost. There's a compile flag we use in bench: -DREDWOOD_PERSIST_THREADS. Worth testing for the first microbatches.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout completed to perf-canary cluster at 1855554300.

devon: Job finished: microbatch=4 + disable fallback + kv-prewarm=sync -> end-to-end latency down ~18%, all-reduce tail reduced by ~25%, kv hit recovered to 0.92. Uploading traces to /perf/artifacts/1855554321/trace.zip and will open a PR.

sasha: Great news. Follow-up plan: re-enable KV prewarm but force sync prewarm for the first N steps, and bias kernel-selector to prefer low-launch-latency kernels for the initial microbatches (then revert to highest-throughput kernels after warmup). We'll also test the split-reduce patch.

maria: Filed perf PR #5123 with traces, experimental flags, and a checklist (staggered warmup, kernel bias, split-reduce). cc @kevin @cheng for review.

sasha: Thanks all — assigning to runtime perf epic. Let's reconvene after the split-reduce vs persistent-thread runs.
